critical_code_review_comments: server.py source_zip filter has an operator-precedence bug: `rel.name == 'yarn.lock' and 'frontend' not in parts` is AND'd into the big `or` chain WITHOUT parens — it currently evaluates as `(... or rel.name == 'yarn.lock') and 'frontend' not in parts`, so when a path has 'frontend' in parts the entire skip predicate becomes False, allowing e.g. frontend/.env to slip through. Today it still works because the earlier clause `rel.name.startswith('.env')` catches .env, but the intent is wrong. Wrap the yarn.lock clause in parentheses.

source_zip() walks the entire repo tree synchronously inside an async endpoint (`for p in root.rglob(...)` + `p.stat()` + ZIP_DEFLATED compression). On a cold request it took ~5–7 s and will block the event loop; move the build into asyncio.to_thread or use fastapi.responses.StreamingResponse with run_in_threadpool.

_SRC_SKIP contains 'build' so the first rglob loop skips frontend/build; the explicit second loop (lines 644–648) adds build/* without the 25 MB size cap or the .env filter — currently harmless (no .env in build) but asymmetrical. Apply the same filters to the explicit build loop.
fisher_price.py is now ~1420 lines (unchanged from iter19 feedback); still above the 700-line split guideline. Split into partition.py and mesh.py.

The CREDITS string in server.py and the hard-coded SCAD prefix in fisher_price.py:1318 duplicate the same text — a single CREDITS import from fisher_price (or vice-versa) would prevent drift between the SCAD header and the mesh-check header.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter20 is a credits/branding + source-zip feature. Backend tests require REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL to be exported before pytest (shell: `export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2)`) — multiple existing suites (test_iter18_voices.py, etc.) read `os.environ.get('REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL','')` with no .env fallback, so they produce MissingSchema errors without the export. The iter19 report mentioned this as flakiness but it is deterministic. UI: a full-screen splash overlay covers the app for ~3 s on EVERY load — always `await page.wait_for_selector("[data-testid='splash-screen']")` then either wait >3.2 s or click to skip before interacting. Important Playwright gotcha: you cannot combine a CSS selector and `text=` locator inside a single string (`"[data-testid='x'], text=Y"`) — use `page.locator("[data-testid='x']").or_(page.get_by_text('Y'))` instead. The /api/source.zip call is slow (~5–7 s) because it walks the whole repo synchronously; give it ≥60 s timeout.
